body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\mu_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]^T}\!\left\{\widehat U(\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat U_{S_c})^{-1}\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat\nu_c\right\},\qquad \mathcal R_N\lesssim\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\},\quad \mathcal W_{N,\alpha}\lesssim\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\), with \(\widehat\theta\) and \(\widehat\rho_N\) defined by robust joint-moment blocks; if a required cohort moment is unavailable or an inverse is singular, the point estimator returns the zero vector. These are unconditional upper guarantees on nonempty shells. A frontier-scale testing pair on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open; \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient, not necessary in the tight-radius zero-target class.

sampling_model.design: Observational short panel with deterministic cohort-specific untreated masks \(S_c\) and independent cross-sectional sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: For cohort \(c\), only \(J_cY_i(0)\) is used for recovery; observed treated outcomes may be appended and are held fixed in countermodels.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \(p_c\ge p_{\star}\) and every \(S_c\) has at least three coordinates; identification strength is \(s(P)\), not pairwise cohort overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The joint cohort indicator, first-moment, and second-moment vector is estimated by coordinatewise median of means with a robust data-driven scale. Covariance PCA supplies the point estimator and its unconditional upper risk bound. Honest inference profiles distance to the compact primitive moment model and inverts a nonempty recentered \(\ell_\infty\) moment set, yielding uniform coverage and an upper width bound without a model-specific lower-width claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 establishes \(O_3\) acceptance as a sufficient mask condition for factor-plane identification.
Their Theorems 1 and 2 supply rank-two deterministic sampling count conditions for generic subspace identification and matrix completion.
Their Theorems 1--3 provide entrywise intervals and an instance-wise lower bound for a growing staggered-block matrix model.
Their weak-factor results derive minimax and honesty costs when factor strength or factor number is uncertain.
Their paper establishes uniformly valid identification-robust tests and confidence sets across weak, semi-strong, and strong sequences in broad extremum models.
Their Theorem 1 and corollaries give deterministic necessary and sufficient conditions for generic coordinate-subspace identifiability.
Their Theorem 1 bounds canonical-projection subspace error by projection noise divided by a relation singular value.
Their Theorems 10 and 12 identify generic entry completability with closure in the determinantal matroid through Jacobian row span.
Their Theorem 1.8 and pebble algorithms characterize and recognize sparse hypergraphs.

body.tldr: Short panels with systematic missing outcomes require gluing cohort-specific covariance eigenspaces before missing untreated means become causal functionals. A deterministic smallest-two anchor convention maps every mask to the published rank-two count certificate of Pimentel--Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak, with Streinu--Theran pebble recognition and extraction as background. When the certificate passes, the observed local eigenspaces determine the global factor plane and an explicit complete-observed-law map recovers every untreated cohort-time mean. When it fails, the factor plane is generically nonunique, but the frozen primitive class does not imply causal-target nonidentification because an allowed tight-radius subclass has \(\mu=0\) throughout. The panel-specific corollary \(O_3\Rightarrow\) certificate acceptance remains strict for masks \(123,145,256,346\). Covariance PCA gives the unconditional squared-risk upper scale \(\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\), and robust profile-recentered moment inversion gives uniformly honest rectangles with upper half-width scale \(\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). Construction of frontier-scale testing pairs on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open; \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient for consistency but is not necessary on the zero-target subclass.

project_justification.gap: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion, Streinu and Theran provide sparse-hypergraph pebble machinery, and Lei and Ross provide \(O_3\)-sufficient identification and regular APM inference. What remains distinct here is the positive causal transport from observed cohort moments through local eigenspaces and the relation kernel to an explicit complete-observed-law functional. Under the frozen primitive class, certificate failure proves factor-plane ambiguity but not different causal-target values, and no model-specific minimax or honest-width lower frontier is currently available.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies fixed-\(T\) causal recovery under deterministic cohort masks, separating generic factor-plane certification from causal-target identification. It combines the published certificate with an explicit observed-law mean functional, the strict panel-specific \(O_3\) containment witness, covariance-PCA upper risk, and finite-moment uniformly honest moment-inversion upper width near a singular relation margin.
project_justification.fill: The paper takes the published count and pebble results as inputs, proves that certificate acceptance yields complete-observed-law identification of every untreated cohort-time mean, and proves that certificate failure yields only generic factor-plane nonuniqueness without further primitive slack. It records strict \(O_3\) containment and develops unconditional covariance-PCA and robust-inversion upper guarantees. Frontier-scale testing-pair construction on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and the corresponding lower risk and width bounds are left open.

body.related_work: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion for generic subspace identification and matrix completion; that rank/count reduction is cited background rather than a novelty claim. Streinu and Theran supply sparse-hypergraph pebble recognition, extraction, component algorithms, and complexity. Király, Theran, and Tomioka identify generic completion through Jacobian closure and determinantal matroids. The distinct causal step here recovers cohort conditional eigenspaces from the complete observed law and proves that certificate acceptance yields an explicit functional for every missing untreated mean; certificate failure is interpreted only as generic factor-plane nonuniqueness. Lei and Ross provide the closest econometric setup: their \(O_3\) overlap-merging condition is sufficient for factor-plane identification and their APM estimator yields regular fixed-\(T\) inference. As a panel-specific corollary, \(O_3\) acceptance implies canonical certificate acceptance, while masks \(123,145,256,346\) are certificate-accepted and \(O_3\)-rejected. Srivastava and Pimentel-Alarcón establish reciprocal-singular-value projection perturbation, which supports the upper analysis but does not furnish a legal target-separating experiment in this frozen model. Yan and Wainwright study growing staggered-block matrices, Zhu studies weak-factor honesty costs, and Andrews and Cheng develop identification-robust inference; none supplies the still-open nondegenerate same-shell testing pair required for lower risk and width frontiers here. Liu, Wang, and Xu provide a concrete consumer through the \(\operatorname{fect}\) counterfactual-imputation workflow.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Certificate failure makes the generic factor plane nonunique, but the frozen primitive class permits tight covariance and moment radii that force every cohort loading mean, and hence every causal target coordinate, to zero. Therefore certificate failure alone does not imply causal-target nonidentification, and \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient but not necessary for consistency on this class. Shell nonemptiness likewise supplies no target separation or primitive interior slack, so construction of a frontier-scale testing pair on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass remains open, as does a model-specific lower bound for uniformly honest rectangle width. The covariance-PCA risk bound and robust profile-inversion honesty and width bounds are unconditional upper results. The profile inversion is an exact optimization over a compact primitive closure; numerical certification is outside the theorem.
body.honest_scope: The smallest-two anchor convention is deterministic, and the rank-two count criterion and pebble algorithms are published background. The paper claims the distinct positive causal transport: certificate acceptance makes every untreated cohort-time mean an explicit functional of the complete observed law. On certificate failure it claims generic nonuniqueness of the factor plane only, not observed-law-equivalent causal targets with different missing means. The panel-specific corollary \(O_3\Rightarrow\) certificate acceptance and its strict four-mask witness remain. Covariance PCA and the total profile-recentered robust moment inversion provide unconditional upper guarantees on nonempty singular-margin shells. The inversion uses an explicit \(\ell_\infty\) joint-moment norm, coordinatewise median-of-means estimation, a data-driven scale, finite-sample coverage, and an eventually empty full-box fallback. No minimax lower frontier, honest-width lower frontier, or necessity of \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is claimed under the frozen class; the required nondegenerate same-shell testing construction remains open.
